reason: The data protection page states ELB terminates HTTPS and TLS traffic at the load balancer, which does the encryption work instead of each EC2 instance.
The pricing page states for ALB, NLB and GWLB each that a partial hour is billed as a full hour, with the hourly charge sentence for the ALB.
The Gateway Load Balancer section states GWLBE, a VPC endpoint type powered by PrivateLink, is priced and billed separately.
Two sections of the pricing page state standard data transfer charges in addition to ELB charges and standard public IPv4 charges for addresses used with load balancers.
The quote says endpoint services require either an NLB or a GWLB, which receives consumer requests and routes them to the service.
The quote states the source IPs seen are the private IPs of the load balancer nodes, and that proxy protocol on the load balancer gives consumer addresses and endpoint IDs.
The ALB quota table row under Default and Adjustable shows 3,000 target groups per Region with Adjustable Yes.
The quota table row shows 1,000 targets per target group per Region (instances or IP addresses), default, adjustable Yes.
The Route 53 related-services text says AWS assigns URLs to resources such as load balancers and you can map your domain name to a load balancer.
The quote states ELB monitors the health of registered targets and routes traffic only to healthy targets.
The quote states ELB scales load balancer capacity automatically in response to changes in incoming traffic.
The Load balancer scheme section says that when you create a load balancer you must choose internal or internet-facing.
The quote states a secure listener needs cipher suites, protocol versions and a server certificate on the load balancer, managed with ACM or IAM.
The quote says Classic Load Balancers support both HTTPS and TLS listeners (present tense); the claim says supported (past tense), which the quote does not state.

The Session Management text calls a centralized session data store the ideal solution for modern architectures, with consistent experiences across web servers and better durability when the fleet is elastic.
The Shield Advanced resource list names NLBs protected through associations to Elastic IP addresses.
The NLB sticky sessions considerations state uneven distribution and the NAT same-source-IP example with all traffic going to the same target.
The DNS failover item states that below the threshold the load balancer node IPs for the zone are marked unhealthy in DNS and traffic goes only to healthy zones.
The Routing failover item states that below the threshold the load balancer sends traffic to all available targets, including unhealthy ones.
Both ALB and NLB pages state the default of healthy with at least one healthy target and that you can specify a minimum count or percentage instead.
The NLB quota footnote on the Target Groups per Region row says the quota is shared by ALBs and NLBs.

The ALB security group considerations state to set the load balancer security group as the source in the target security group ingress rule so targets receive traffic exclusively from the load balancer.
The quote states targets registered in an Availability Zone that is not enabled do not receive traffic.
The quote states both scheme types route to targets using private IPs, so targets need no public IPs.
The quote is from the Application Load Balancer security policies page; the claim says load balancer listeners in general without limiting it to ALB.
The quote states the load balancer stops routing to an unhealthy target and resumes when it detects the target is healthy again.
REL10-BP01 states that if you disable cross-zone load balancing, use ARC to provide zonal shift capability.
REL10-BP01 states that with cross-zone enabled, ALBs and NLBs detect unreachable targets from an AZ impairment and reroute to healthy AZs.
REL10-BP01 says to place load balancers in front of compute resources and, in the preceding step, to deploy compute into multiple Availability Zones.
SEC09-BP02 says to allow only secure protocols and gives the example of a security group allowing only HTTPS to an application load balancer or EC2 instance.
The ELB FAQ says an ALB can integrate with AWS WAF using rules on IP addresses, HTTP headers and URI strings to block, allow or count requests.
The ALB forward-action quote gives only the 0 to 999 range; weight 0 receiving no traffic is stated only on the NLB listeners page, so the claim joins two services.
The quote states ELB automatically distributes incoming traffic across targets such as EC2 instances, containers and IPs in one or more Availability Zones.
The quote states with zonal autoshift you authorize AWS to shift traffic away from an AZ on your behalf, started when internal monitoring indicates an impairment that could impact customers.
The quote states that with cross-zone off a zonal shift removing a zonal IP also removes target capacity in that AZ, and to always check capacity first.
The quote and its context state the load balancer stops sending new traffic to the AZ and existing connections can take a short time to complete.
The quote states zonal shift is an ARC feature that shifts traffic away from an impaired AZ with a single action so you continue from healthy AZs.
